L172: # ImageData
L173: 
L174: Baseline
L175: 
L176: Widely available
L177: 
L178: *
L179: 
L180: This feature is well established and works across many devices and browser versions. It’s been available across browsers since July 2015.
L181: 
L182: * Some parts of this feature may have varying levels of support.
L183: 
L184:   * 【86†See full compatibility】
L185:   * 【87†Learn more】
L186: 
L187: Note: This feature is available in 【88†Web Workers】.
L188: 
L189: The `ImageData` interface represents the underlying pixel data of an area of a 【89†`<canvas>`】 element.
L190: It is created using the 【90†`ImageData()`】 constructor or creator methods on the 【91†`CanvasRenderingContext2D`】 object associated with a canvas: 【92†`createImageData()`】 and 【93†`getImageData()`】. It can also be used to set a part of the canvas by using 【94†`putImageData()`】.
L191: ## In this article
L192: 
L193:   * 【95†Constructors】
L194:   * 【96†Instance properties】
L195:   * 【97†Specifications】
L196:   * 【86†Browser compatibility】
L197:   * 【98†See also】
L198: ## 【95†Constructors】
L199: 
L200: 【90†`ImageData()`】
L201: 
L202: 
L203: Creates an `ImageData` object from a given 【99†`Uint8ClampedArray`】 or 【100†`Float16Array`】 and the size of the image it contains. If no array is given, it creates an image of a transparent black rectangle. Note that this is the most common way to create such an object in workers as 【92†`createImageData()`】 is not available there.
L204: ## 【96†Instance properties】
L205: 
L206: 【101†`ImageData.data`】 Read only
L207: 
L208: 
L209: A 【99†`Uint8ClampedArray`】 or 【100†`Float16Array`】 representing a one-dimensional array containing the data in the RGBA order. The order goes by rows from the top-left pixel to the bottom-right.
L210: 
L211: 【102†`ImageData.colorSpace`】 Read only
L212: 
L213: 
L214: A string indicating the color space of the image data.
L215: 
L216: 【103†`ImageData.height`】 Read only
L217: 
L218: 
L219: An `unsigned long` representing the actual height, in pixels, of the `ImageData`.
L220: 【104†`ImageData.width`】 Read only
L221: 
L222: 
L223: An `unsigned long` representing the actual width, in pixels, of the `ImageData`.
L224: 
L225: 【105†`ImageData.pixelFormat`】 Read only
L226: 
L227: 
L228: A string indicating the format to use for the `ImageData`.

L27: ## 9.1. Introduction
L28: 
L29: A path represents the outline of a shape which can be filled or stroked. A path can also be used as a clipping path, to describe animation, or position text. A path can be used for more than one of these functions at the same time. (See 【29†Filling, Stroking and Paint Servers】, 【30†Clipping and Masking】, Animation (【31†'animateMotion'†w3c.github.io】), and 【32†Text on a Path】.)
L30: A path is described using the concept of a current point. In an analogy with drawing on paper, the current point can be thought of as the location of the pen. The position of the pen can be changed, and the outline of a shape (open or closed) can be traced by dragging the pen in either straight lines or curves.
L31: Paths represent the geometry of the outline of an object, defined in terms of moveto (set a new current point), lineto (draw a straight line), curveto (draw a curve using a cubic Bézier), arc (elliptical or circular arc) and closepath (close the current shape by connecting to the last moveto) commands. Compound paths (i.e., a path with multiple subpaths) are possible to allow effects such as "donut holes" in objects.
L32: This chapter describes the syntax, behavior and DOM interfaces for SVG paths. Various implementation notes for SVG paths can be found in 【19†‘path’ element implementation Notes】.
L33: 
L34: A path is defined in SVG using the ‘【7†path】’ element.
L35: 
L36: The 【33†basic shapes】 are all described in terms of what their equivalent path is, which is what their shape is as a path. (The equivalent path of a ‘【7†path】’ element is simply the path itself.)

L64: ## 9.3. Path data
L65: ### 9.3.1. General information about path data
L66: 
L67: A path is defined by including a ‘【7†path】’ element on which the 【118†d】 property specifies the path data. The path data contains the moveto, lineto, curveto (both cubic and quadratic Béziers), arc and closepath instructions.
L68: Example triangle01 specifies a path in the shape of a triangle. (The M indicates a moveto, the Ls indicate linetos, and the z indicates a closepath).

L70:     <?xml version="1.0" standalone="no"?>
L71:     <svg width="4cm" height="4cm" viewBox="0 0 400 400"
L72:          xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" version="1.1">
L73:       <title>Example triangle01- simple example of a 'path'</title>
L74:       <desc>A path that draws a triangle</desc>
L75:       <rect x="1" y="1" width="398" height="398"
L76:             fill="none" stroke="blue" />
L77:       <path d="M 100 100 L 300 100 L 200 300 z"
L78:             fill="red" stroke="blue" stroke-width="3" />
L79:     </svg>

L86: Path data can contain newline characters and thus can be broken up into multiple lines to improve readability. Newlines inside attributes in markup will be normalized to space characters while parsing.
L87: The syntax of path data is concise in order to allow for minimal file size and efficient downloads, since many SVG files will be dominated by their path data. Some of the ways that SVG attempts to minimize the size of path data are as follows:
L88: 
L89:   * All instructions are expressed as one character (e.g., a moveto is expressed as an M).
L90:   * Superfluous white space and separators (such as commas) may be eliminated; for instance, the following contains unnecessary spaces:
L91: 
L92: `M 100 100 L 200 200`
L93: It may be expressed more compactly as:
L94: 
L95: `M100 100L200 200`
L96: 
L97:   * A command letter may be eliminated if an identical command letter would otherwise precede it; for instance, the following contains an unnecessary second "L" command:
L98: 
L99: `M 100 200 L 200 100 L -100 -200`
L100: 
L101: It may be expressed more compactly as:
L102: 
L103: `M 100 200 L 200 100 -100 -200`
L104:   * For most commands there are absolute and relative versions available (uppercase means absolute coordinates, lowercase means relative coordinates).
L105:   * Alternate forms of lineto are available to optimize the special cases of horizontal and vertical lines (absolute and relative).
L106:   * Alternate forms of curve are available to optimize the special cases where some of the control points on the current segment can be determined automatically from the control points on the previous segment.
L107: The path data syntax is a prefix notation (i.e., commands followed by parameters). The only allowable decimal point is a Unicode U+002E FULL STOP (".") character (also referred to in Unicode as PERIOD, dot and decimal point) and no other delimiter characters are allowed [【121†UNICODE】]. (For example, the following is an invalid numeric value in a path data stream: "13,000.56". Instead, say: "13000.56".)
L108: For the relative versions of the commands, all coordinate values are relative to the current point at the start of the command.
L109: 
L110: In the tables below, the following notation is used to describe the syntax of a given path command:
L111: 
L112:   * (): grouping of parameters
L113:   * +: 1 or more of the given parameter(s) is required
L114: 
L115: In the description of the path commands, `cpx` and `cpy` represent the coordinates of the current point.
L116: ### 9.3.2. Specifying path data: the ‘d’ property
L117: 
L118: Name:  | d
L119: Value:  | none | 【122†<string>】
L120: Initial:  | none
L121: Applies to:  | ‘【7†path】’
L122: Inherited:  | no
L123: Percentages:  | N/A
L124: Media:  | visual
L125: Computed value:  | as specified
L126: 【123†Animation type】:  | See prose
L127: 
L128: The 【118†d】 property is used to specify the shape of a ‘【7†path】’ element.
L129: The value none indicates that there is no path data for the element. For ‘【7†path】’ elements, this means that the element does not render or contribute to the 【124†bounding box】 of ancestor 【125†container elements】.
L130: 
L131: A path is made up of multiple segments, and every command, either explicit or implicit, other than moveto or closepath, defines one path segment.
L132: 
L133: All coordinates and lengths specified within path data must be treated as being in 【126†user units】 in the current user coordinate system.
L134: The 【122†<string>】 value specifies a shape using a path data string. The contents of the 【122†<string>】 value must match the 【17†svg-path】 【127†EBNF grammar】 defined below, and errors within the string are handled according to the rules in the 【23†Path Data Error Handling】 section. If the path data string contains no valid commands, then the behavior is the same as the none value.
L135: For animation, two 【118†d】 property values can only be interpolated smoothly when the path data strings contain have the same structure, (i.e. exactly the same number and types of path data commands which are in the same order). If an animation is specified and the lists of path data commands do not have the same structure, then the values must be 【128†interpolated†drafts.csswg.org】 using the 【129†discrete†drafts.csswg.org】 animation type.
L136: For 【130†from†svgwg.org】/【131†by†svgwg.org】 animations or 【132†additive†svgwg.org】 animations, if the specified animation values are incompatible (i.e. the path data command lists do not have the same structure), then the animation must not produce an effect value. The element must render using the base value for the duration of the animation and after the animation ends. In particular, when ‘fill’='freeze' is specified, the frozen value must be the base value.
L137: A 【131†by†svgwg.org】 animation is additive by definition, so when the base value's path data command list is incompatible with the 【131†by†svgwg.org】 value, additive composition is undefined; see 【133†SMIL Animation: from, to, by and additive behavior】.
L138: If the list of path data commands have the same structure, then each parameter to each path data command must be 【128†interpolated†drafts.csswg.org】 separately 【134†as real numbers†drafts.csswg.org】. Flags and booleans must be interpolated as fractions between zero and one, with any non-zero value considered to be a value of one/true.
L139: 
L140: Resolved that "d will become a presentation attribute (no name change) with path data string as value" at 【135†London Editor's Meeting】.
L141: The following sections list the commands that can be used in path data strings. Those that draw straight line segments include the 【13†lineto commands】 (L, l, H, h, V and v) and the 【12†close path commands】 (Z and z). These three groups of commands draw curves:
L142:   * 【14†Cubic Bézier commands】 (C, c, S and s). A cubic Bézier segment is defined by a start point, an end point, and two control points.
